rationale: Of the machines in this batch, #10 is the closest to a kill. The rule layer is exact and its L1 lemmas are written (check_proof.py revision 2: all checks pass). The epoch map has a closed form that reproduces 1,142 of 1,142 TM epochs to 1e11 steps. Proved lemmas (the cascade lemma, Lemma Z and Lemma R) reduce non-halting to one statement about the epochs after an excursion. The data favour a finite case analysis. Excursions are rare and short: at most 2 epochs on natural orbits and 4 in constructed ones. Of 1,087 excursion entries in check 7, 1,052 follow a cascade. In a separate scratch run, 125 of 127 did, and the other 2 followed a near-cascade of the kind the plan names. There are 0 violations in 6M eats on other orbits, in the skeptic's 2e9 eats, on the main orbit to 1e10 epochs and in 324,956 constructed cascade starts. Every case examined is excluded by exact arithmetic, which is not what a cryptid looks like. The honest risk is that the entry types do not form a small list. Magnitude bounds provably cannot prove Lemma X (the super-cascade shows this), and arbitrary starts do violate, which is why the stage has a hard exit to the cryptid flag. A success also covers the trajectory twin 1RB0RE_1RC1RE_1LD1RA_1LA0LD_0RA0LF_1LD---.

In a separate scratch run, 125 of 127 did, and the 2 others followed a near-cascade. 0 violations in 324,956 constructed cascade and near-cascade starts.

Magnitude bounds cannot prove Lemma X: the super-cascade at n=1019 gives slack -1. Arbitrary starts also violate (two are confirmed on the TM). So the proof must describe the reachable residues exactly.
